issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be rejected at the threshold when a meaningful reading of its allegations, taken at face value, shows that none of the reliefs claimed is legally available.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought declarations concerning the partnership firm's assets and representation of the firm, injunctions, accounts, and dissolution.
The plaintiffs claimed through deceased partners but were not themselves partners; the pleaded facts also described the firm as continuing its business.
The court assessed whether the pleaded reliefs could be granted without considering the defendants’ defence and agreed that none could be granted in law.
issues.conclusion: The plaint was properly rejected, and the appeals challenging that rejection were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII Rule 11(a) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court must scrutinise the plaint’s averments, read meaningfully and as a whole, together with documents relied on, to determine whether it discloses a cause of action; the defence is not considered. If the reliefs claimed cannot be granted on the pleaded facts, the suit need not proceed to trial. The court relied on T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal, Pearlite Liners (P) Ltd. v. Manorama Sirsi, and Dahiben v. Arvindbhai Kalyanji Bhanusali; Dahiben also referred to Azhar Hussain v. Rajiv Gandhi and Liverpool & London S.P. & I Assn. Ltd. v. M.V. Sea Success I. The power is drastic and the conditions for its exercise must be strictly followed.

predicates.application_to_reject_plaint: A party applied for rejection of a plaint in a civil suit.
predicates.plaint_assessed_on_its_averments: The court assessed the pleaded allegations at face value, without relying on the opposing party’s defence.
predicates.every_claimed_relief_unavailable: The pleaded facts leave none of the reliefs requested legally available to the claimant.

issues.definition: When a rejection application concerns a plaint assessed on its allegations and every requested relief is unavailable on those allegations, the plaint is rejected at the threshold.

issues.legal_issue: Heirs of partners cannot claim direct ownership of the assets of a partnership firm that is continuing its business.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed entitlement to the firm’s assets as heirs of deceased original partners.
The firm was pleaded to have continued its business after the deaths of the original partners.
The plaintiffs sought a declaration that they and the defendants were entitled to the firm’s assets and properties.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs, as heirs who were not partners, could not maintain a claim to co-ownership of the assets of the continuing firm.
issues.legal_principle: The court agreed with the High Court’s stated principle that partners are entitled to the profits of a firm and, upon dissolution, to any surplus remaining after the firm’s liabilities are met; while the firm continues its business, partners do not have individual title to its assets. The judgment states this as settled partnership law and does not identify a particular earlier case or provision as the basis for this specific asset-ownership principle.

predicates.claim_for_direct_ownership_of_firm_asset: The claimants seek direct ownership of assets held by a partnership firm.
predicates.claimants_are_heirs_not_partners: The claimants derive their claims from deceased partners but are not themselves partners.
predicates.firm_continues_business: The partnership firm continues to carry on its business.

issues.definition: Heirs who are not partners cannot claim direct ownership of firm assets when the firm continues its business.

issues.legal_issue: A non-partner cannot sue for dissolution of a partnership firm or seek accounts for the purpose of that dissolution.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought a decree dissolving the firm and winding up its affairs, together with accounts for the purpose of dissolution.
The plaintiffs were heirs of deceased partners and were not partners themselves.
The partnership deed provided that a partner’s death did not automatically dissolve the partnership, and the firm was pleaded to have continued its business.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs could not obtain dissolution of the firm or accounts for the purpose of dissolution because they were not partners.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 39 to 44 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, address dissolution: Section 40 provides for dissolution by agreement, Section 42 makes dissolution on specified contingencies subject to contract, Section 43 concerns dissolution of a partnership at will, and Section 44 empowers the court to dissolve a firm at the suit of a partner on specified grounds. The court agreed that a non-partner cannot seek court-ordered dissolution and consequently cannot seek accounts for the purpose of such dissolution. It relied on the partnership deed’s provision that death would not automatically dissolve the firm; no earlier case was cited for this holding.

predicates.suit_seeks_firm_dissolution_or_dissoluti: The claimants bring a suit seeking dissolution of a partnership firm or accounts for the purpose of dissolving it.
predicates.claimants_are_not_partners: The claimants are not partners in the firm.

issues.definition: A claimant who is not a partner cannot obtain court-ordered dissolution or accounts sought for that dissolution.
